newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong welcomes U.S. extradition order.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong welcomes U.S. extradition order.

text.p: Hong Kong's anti-graft watchdog said on Saturday it welcomed a decision by a U.S. federal appeals court ordering the extradition of a fugitive to the British colony.

Thursday's decision by the court in Boston overturned an earlier ruling by a district court judge who blocked the return of Jerry Lui Kin-hong, who faces multimillion dollar bribery and conspiracy charges in Hong Kong relating to cigarette smuggling.

"The commission welcomes the decision of the U.S. Court of Appeals in favour of the U.S. Attorney's office, who are seeking Lui's extradition to Hong Kong on behalf of the Hong Kong government," Hong Kong's Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) said in a statement.
"We hope Lui would be returned to the territory as soon as possible to face trial," it said in a statement.

Boston District Court Judge Joseph Tauro earlier this year blocked Lui's extradition after defence lawyers argued that he faced possible execution if forced to return to Hong Kong as his trial was unlikely to be completed before the handover of the colony to China on July 1.
Tauro's decision raised a furore in Hong Kong and was seen as undermining efforts to convince the world it will retain judicial independence after the handover.
The U.S. government said it disagreed wit Tauro and was considering appealing against his decision.
The ICAC declined to estimate when Lui might be returned as the timing depended on whether he would appeal against the federal court ruling. He has to do so within 14 days.
"If he doesn't appeal within the 14 days, then he'll return after all the necessary papers are signed," an ICAC spokeswoman told Reuters.
Lui was arrested at Boston's Logan International Airport when he flew there from Canada to visit a sick friend in December 1995.
